tips.title: The Two-Cut Method with GodHand Ultimate Nippers
tips.text: GodHand Ultimate Nippers have razor-sharp edges that leave almost no stress mark, but they are fragile and will chip if used on thick gates. Use the two-cut method: first cut the gate 2mm from the part with cheaper single-action nippers, then make the final flush cut with the GodHand. Never twist or pull the part off — always cut straight through. This works especially well on delicate Eduard photo-etch frets and Clear Prop Models canopy parts.

tips.title: Scribing Panel Lines with RB Productions Tools
tips.text: Panel lines on plastic kits can be shallow. Use RB Productions' line scriber or 'U' tool to deepen them. Hold the tool at a 45° angle to the surface, applying gentle pressure. Start from the middle of the panel and work outwards to avoid fracturing the plastic. For complex curves, use the 'U' tool to follow the line precisely. Suitable for kits like ICM and Arma Hobby.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning with Iwata's Cleaner and Thinner
tips.text: Regularly clean your Iwata airbrush needle to maintain consistent paint flow. First, remove the needle chuck and needle using the appropriate wrench. Then, soak the needle in Iwata Cleaner and Thinner for 10-15 minutes. Gently scrub with an old toothbrush, rinse with clean thinner, and dry thoroughly before reassembly. This prevents clogs and ensures smooth paint delivery.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya tape vs Kabuki tape
tips.text: For complex shapes, use Tamiya tape for its strong adhesion and ease of handling. For fine details and intricate patterns, opt for Kabuki tape due to its thinner profile and better conformability. Apply Tamiya tape in longer strips, pressing firmly to avoid bubbles. For Kabuki, use short pieces and gently press down to avoid creasing. Both tapes require a sharp knife for trimming and should be applied over a light coat of Vallejo Airbrush Thinner to improve adhesion.

tips.title: Sanding Sticks Progression for Smooth Surfaces
tips.text: Sanding sticks help achieve smooth surfaces on large areas. Start with 220 grit for coarse sanding, followed by 320 grit for smoothing. For optimal results, use Tamiya Fine Surface 5000 and 8000 grit polishing compounds after sanding. Wet-sand using water or Tamiya Surface Primer Thinner for better control and fewer dust particles. Always sand in straight lines and follow the direction of panel lines for the best finish.
